@keep_lazy_text
def wrap(text, width):
    """
    A word-wrap function that preserves existing line breaks. Expects that
    existing line breaks are posix newlines.

    Preserve all white space except added line breaks consume the space on
    which they break the line.

    Don't wrap long words, thus the output text may have lines longer than
    ``width``.
    """
    
    import textwrap

    def wordwrap(text, width):

            width=width,

        for line in text.splitlines(True):

            # Preserve leading whitespace for each line
            formatted_lines = [line if not line.strip() else ' ' + line.lstrip() for line in lines]
            result.extend(formatted_lines)
        return "\n".join(result)

    return wordwrap(text, width)

@keep_lazy_text
def wrap(text, width):
    """
    A word-wrap function that preserves existing line breaks. Expects that
    existing line breaks are posix newlines.

    Preserve all white space except added line breaks consume the space on
    which they break the line.

    Don't wrap long words, thus the output text may have lines longer than
    ``width``.
    """
    
    import textwrap

    def wordwrap(text, width):
        wrapper = textwrap.TextWrapper(
            width=width,
            break_long_words=False,
            break_on_hyphens=False,
            replace_whitespace=False,  # Preserve existing whitespace
            drop_whitespace=False  # Preserve existing whitespace
        )
        result = []
        for line in text.splitlines(True):
            lines = wrapper.wrap(line)
            # Preserve leading whitespace for each line
            formatted_lines = [line if not line.strip() else ' ' + line.lstrip() for line in lines]
            result.extend(formatted_lines)
        return "".join(result)

    return wordwrap(text, width)
